name: TranStar (1986)
description: TranStar's only scheme: the whole aircraft a deep navy blue, nose to tail and fin and nacelles. 'TranStar' in light blue serif letters, big and low on the forward fuselage under the first windows. Thin pinstripes slant down and forward across the rear of the body, from the crown to the belly, in order from the front pink, green, light blue and pink, about 3 m apart, with a fifth in green running down the fin from near its tip to the tail cone. They carry on across the nacelles. Gray wings, bare metal inlet lips.

notes: Measured 2026-11-26 for ghost flights on MD-82 N935MC (June 1986, right side) on shapes/MD82.json, checked on the MD-80 of March 1986 from the left, with the DC-9-51 measured as a type on N675MC (October 1986). TranStar was Muse Air renamed in February 1986 under Southwest and this was its only scheme: dated photos from March 1986 to March 1987 all show it. Every stripe is a straight line in the side view, crossing the window line (0.365 m up) at its measured place and rising aft at its measured slope, about 0.1 m wide; on the MD-80 they cross the window line at 26.0, 28.7, 31.8 and 34.7 m and the fin's at 37.2 m. Where a stripe passes a nacelle it is carried across it on the same line. The navy reads near black in low sun and royal blue in bright sun; the rudder of N935MC shines gold in its June 1986 photo, a reflection: the same rudder is blue on the other photos. No logo was found. A small red marking low on the tail cone isn't drawn. The pinstripes' exact shades are read off color film.

DC95.note: DC-9-51 N675MC (October 1986), side-on from the right, checked on N672MC: the title from 5.2 m back, 7.1 m long, capitals 1.2 m, its foot 1.2 m under the centerline; the stripes cross the window line at 22.0, 25.2, 28.3 and 31.3 m, the fin's at 34.4 m, each rising 0.75 m aft per meter up. Within about 0.15 m.
